pll1d46c2-d1e3509.summary: Turns to the solution, first of the Lord's words in Matt 23:37.

pll1d46c2-d1e3514.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: it does not mean the Lord willed to gather Jerusalem's children and failed because she would not; rather, she did not will her children gathered, yet against her will he gathered all he willed. 'How often I willed...' means: as many as I gathered by my ever-effective will, I gathered against your will.
claims: God gathered all he willed, against Jerusalem's will.

pll1d46c2-d1e3553.summary: Concludes that the Lord's words do not contradict what was said.
claims: Matt 23:37 is consistent with God's omnipotent will.

pll1d46c2-d1e3558.summary: Turns to 1 Tim 2:4, which led many to say God wills much that does not happen; it should not be understood as if God willed some to be saved and they were not.
claims: 1 Tim 2:4 does not mean God's will fails.

pll1d46c2-d1e3573.summary: Continues Augustine: who would be so impiously foolish as to say God cannot turn evil wills to good when and where he wills? 'He did all he willed' would be false if he willed something and did not, worse if because human will impeded the Omnipotent.
claims: God can turn evil wills to good.
Human will cannot impede the Omnipotent.

pll1d46c2-d1e3597.summary: Further Augustine: 'he wills all to be saved' means no one is saved unless God wills it, not that there is no one he does not will saved; so he must be prayed to will it, since if he wills, it must happen. Similarly 'he enlightens every man' means no one is enlightened except by him. Other readings are possible provided we do not believe the Omnipotent willed what did not happen.
claims: No one is saved unless God wills it.
If God wills something, it must happen.
God never willed what did not happen.

pll1d46c2-d1e3638.summary: Concludes that by the will that he is, God wills nothing to be done that is not done, nor not done that is done.

pl-l1d46c2.summary: Resolves both texts with Augustine's Enchiridion. Matt 23:37 does not mean God willed to gather Jerusalem's children and failed because she would not; rather she did not will her children gathered, yet against her will he gathered all he willed. 1 Tim 2:4 has led many to say God wills much that does not happen, but no one should say God cannot turn evil wills to good when and where he wills. It means no one is saved except whom God wills to be saved, as 'he enlightens every man' means no one is enlightened except by him. It may be read in other ways, provided we do not believe the Omnipotent willed something that did not happen. So by the will that he is, God wills nothing done that is not done, and nothing not done that is done.
claims: God gathered all he willed despite Jerusalem's refusal.
God can turn evil human wills to good when and where he wills.
'God wills all to be saved' means no one is saved unless God wills it.
The Omnipotent never wills anything that does not happen.
By his will (good pleasure), God wills nothing done that is not done.
